sentences.zh: 山濤

translations.literal: Shan Tao.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Tao

sentences.zh: 山濤，字巨源，河內懷人也。

translations.literal: Shan Tao, courtesy name Juyuan, was a man of Huai in Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Tao, courtesy name Juyuan, came from Huai in Henei commandery.

sentences.zh: 父曜，宛句令。

translations.literal: His father Yao was magistrate of Yuanju.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shan Yao had been magistrate of Yuanju.

sentences.zh: 濤早孤，居貧，少有器量，介然不群。

translations.literal: Tao early was orphaned, dwelt poor; in youth had capacity and tolerance—distinct not herd.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young and poor, he showed unusual breadth of character and stood apart from ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 性好《莊》《老》，每隱身自晦。

translations.literal: By nature loved Zhuangzi and Laozi—often concealed body and dimmed himself.
translations.idiomatic: He loved Zhuangzi and Laozi and kept deliberately out of the spotlight.

sentences.zh: 與嵇康、呂安善，後遇阮籍，便為竹林之交，著忘言之契。

translations.literal: With Xi Kang and Lu An was good; later met Ruan Ji—then became Bamboo Grove friendship—established word-forgetting bond.
translations.idiomatic: He befriended Xi Kang and Lu An, then Ruan Ji, forming the Bamboo Grove circle bound by understanding deeper than words.

sentences.zh: 康後坐事，臨誅，謂子紹曰：「巨源在，汝不孤矣。」

translations.literal: Kang later sat crime—facing execution—said to son Shao: "When Juyuan is present, you will not be orphaned."
translations.idiomatic: When Xi Kang faced execution for his crimes, he told his son Xi Shao, "As long as Juyuan lives, you will not stand alone."

sentences.zh: 濤年四十，始為郡主簿、功曹、上計掾。

translations.literal: Tao age forty—first became commandery chief clerk, merit evaluator, clerk for presenting accounts.
translations.idiomatic: At forty he took his first posts—chief clerk, merit officer, and accounting clerk for the commandery.

sentences.zh: 舉孝廉，州辟部河南從事。

translations.literal: Recommended filial and incorrupt—province summoned section Henan attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as filial and incorrupt, he was summoned to serve as staff supervisor for Henan.

sentences.zh: 與石鑒共宿，濤夜起蹴鑒曰：「今為何等時而眠邪！

translations.literal: Lodging with Shi Jian—Tao night rose kicked Jian saying: "Now is what kind of time yet sleeping!"
translations.idiomatic: Sharing lodgings with Shi Jian, Shan Tao woke him with a kick: "How can you sleep at a time like this?"

sentences.zh: 知太傅臥何意？

translations.literal: Know grand tutor lying what intent?
translations.idiomatic: Do you know why the grand tutor lies idle?"

sentences.zh: 」鑒曰：「宰相三不朝，與尺一令歸第，卿何慮也！

translations.literal: Jian said: "Prime minister three times not attending court—with foot-one edict returned mansion—what worry!"
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jian replied, "The chief minister has skipped three audiences and received an edict to go home—what is there to fret about?"

sentences.zh: 」濤曰：「咄！

translations.literal: Tao said: "Tsk!"
translations.idiomatic: Shan Tao snapped, "Nonsense!"

sentences.zh: 石生無事馬蹄間邪！

translations.literal: Mr. Shi nothing affairs between horse hooves!
translations.idiomatic: Master Shi, have you nothing better to do than idle between the horses' hooves?"

sentences.zh: 」投傳而去。

translations.literal: Cast credential and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He threw down his travel permit and left.

sentences.zh: 未二年，果有曹爽之事，遂隱身不交世務。

translations.literal: Not yet two years—indeed had Cao Shuang affair—thereupon concealed body not mingling worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Within two years Cao Shuang fell; Shan Tao withdrew from public life.

sentences.zh: 與宣穆後有中表親，是以見景帝。

translations.literal: With Empress Xuanmu had cousin kin—thereby saw Emperor Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Kinship with Empress Dowager Xuanmu brought him to Emperor Jing's notice.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「呂望欲仕邪？

translations.literal: Emperor said: "Lu Wang desires office?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Do you wish to serve like Lü Wang?"

sentences.zh: 」命司隸舉秀才，除郎中。

translations.literal: Ordered metropolitan commandant raise flourishing talent—appointed gentleman of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Shan Tao recommended as a cultivated talent and appointed gentleman of the palace.

sentences.zh: 轉驃騎將軍王昶從事中郎。

translations.literal: Transferred aide-de-camp to General of Agile Cavalry Wang Chang.
translations.idiomatic: He became aide-de-camp to General of Agile Cavalry Wang Chang.

sentences.zh: 久之，拜趙國相，遷尚書吏部郎。

translations.literal: After long time—appointed Zhao kingdom chancellor—promoted gentleman of Personnel in Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: After long service he became chancellor of Zhao state, then Personnel secretary in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 文帝與濤書曰：「足下在事清明，雅操邁時。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen wrote Tao: "You in affairs clear bright—refined conduct surpasses age."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wen of Wei wrote: "In office you are lucid and upright; your conduct towers above your contemporaries."

sentences.zh: 念多所乏，今致錢二十萬、穀二百斛。

translations.literal: Thinking much lacks—now send cash two hundred thousand, grain two hundred hu.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing your wants are many, I send two hundred thousand cash and two hundred hu of grain."

sentences.zh: 」魏帝嘗賜景帝春服，帝以賜濤。

translations.literal: Wei emperor once granted Emperor Jing spring robes—emperor thereby granted Tao.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei emperor gave Prince Jing spring robes, he passed them on to Shan Tao.

sentences.zh: 又以母老，並賜藜杖一枚。

translations.literal: Also because mother old—together granted one chenopodium staff.
translations.idiomatic: Because his mother was aged, he also received a goosefoot staff of honor.

sentences.zh: 晚與尚書和逌交，又與鐘會、裴秀並申款昵。

translations.literal: Late with vice director He You associated—also with Zhong Hui, Pei Xiu together extended sincere intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: Later he grew close to vice director He You and formed warm ties with Zhong Hui and Pei Xiu.

sentences.zh: 以二人居勢爭權，濤平心處中，各得其所，而俱無恨焉。

translations.literal: Because two men held power contended authority—Tao level heart dwelt middle—each obtained their place—yet both without resentment.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhong Hui and Pei Xiu jockeyed for power, Shan Tao stayed even-handed so both felt satisfied and neither bore a grudge.

sentences.zh: 遷大將軍從事中郎。

translations.literal: Promoted aide-de-camp to grand general.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted aide-de-camp to the grand general.

sentences.zh: 鐘會作亂於蜀，而文帝將西征。

translations.literal: Zhong Hui made rebellion in Shu—yet Emperor Wen would west campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhong Hui rebelled in Shu, Prince Wen prepared a western campaign.

sentences.zh: 時魏氏諸王公並在鄴，帝謂濤曰：「西偏吾自了之，後事深以委卿。

translations.literal: At time Wei clan various princes dukes together at Ye—emperor told Tao: "West flank I self finish—after affairs deeply entrust you."
translations.idiomatic: With Wei princes gathered at Ye, Prince Wen told Shan Tao, "I shall handle the west myself; I leave what follows chiefly to you."

sentences.zh: 」以本官行軍司馬，給親兵五百人，鎮鄴。

translations.literal: In base office acted army marshal—given personal troops five hundred men—garrison Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Tao served as army marshal in his existing rank with five hundred household guards to secure Ye.

sentences.zh: 咸熙初，封新遝子。

translations.literal: Xianxi beginning—enfeoffed Baron of Xintao.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianxi era he was enfeoffed as baron of Xintao.

sentences.zh: 轉相國左長史，典統別營。

translations.literal: Transferred minister of state's chief clerk of left—supervised commanded separate camp.
translations.idiomatic: He became senior clerk on the left under the minister of state and commanded a separate camp.

sentences.zh: 時帝以濤鄉閭宿望，命太子拜之。

translations.literal: At time emperor because Tao village long-standing renown—ordered heir apparent bow to him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Shan Tao enjoyed renown in his home region, the prince ordered the heir apparent to bow to him.

sentences.zh: 帝以齊王攸繼景帝后，素又重攸，嘗問裴秀曰：「大將軍開建未遂，吾但承奉後事耳。

translations.literal: Emperor because Prince Qi You succeeded Emperor Jing—always also esteemed You—once asked Pei Xiu: "Grand general founding establishment not yet completed—I only inherit attend after affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Because Prince You of Qi stood in Emperor Jing's line and the prince favored him, Sima Zhao once asked Pei Xiu, "The grand foundation is unfinished; I only carry on what follows."

sentences.zh: 故立攸，將歸功於兄，何如？

translations.literal: Therefore establish You—will return merit to elder brother—how?
translations.idiomatic: What if I establish You as heir and credit my elder brother?"

sentences.zh: 」秀以為不可，又以問濤。

translations.literal: Xiu deemed not acceptable—again asked Tao.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xiu opposed the idea, so he turned to Shan Tao.

sentences.zh: 濤對曰：「廢長立少，違禮不祥。

translations.literal: Tao replied: "Abolish elder establish younger—violates ritual inauspicious."
translations.idiomatic: Shan Tao answered, "Setting aside the elder for the younger breaks ritual and invites ill fortune."

sentences.zh: 國之安危，恆必由之。

translations.literal: State's peace peril—always necessarily by this.
translations.idiomatic: A state's rise or fall often hinges on such choices."

sentences.zh: 」太子位於是乃定。

translations.literal: Heir apparent position thereby then fixed.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent's place was settled."

sentences.zh: 太子親拜謝濤。

translations.literal: Heir apparent personally bowed thanking Tao.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent bowed to Shan Tao in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 及武帝受禪，以濤守大鴻臚，護送陳留王詣鄴。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu received abdication—made Tao acting grand herald—escorted King of Chenliu to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication, Shan Tao served as acting grand herald escorting the Chenliu king to Ye.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，加奉車都尉，進爵新遝伯。

translations.literal: Taishi beginning—added commandant of palace carriage attendants—advanced rank Earl of Xintao.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taishi he received the title commandant of carriage attendants and advanced to earl of Xintao.

sentences.zh: 及羊祜執政，時人欲危裴秀，濤正色保持之。

translations.literal: When Yang Hu held government—people of time wished endanger Pei Xiu—Tao stern color preserved him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Hu directed the government and others threatened Pei Xiu, Shan Tao defended him sternly.

sentences.zh: 由是失權臣意，出為冀州刺史，加甯遠將軍。

translations.literal: Thereby lost powerful minister's intent—went out as Ji Province governor—added general who pacifies the distance.
translations.idiomatic: That cost him powerful men's favor; he became governor of Ji Province with title general who pacifies the distance.

sentences.zh: 冀州俗薄，無相推轂。

translations.literal: Ji Province customs thin—none mutually push carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Ji customs were mean-spirited; men seldom recommended others.

sentences.zh: 濤甄拔隱屈，搜訪賢才，旌命三十餘人，皆顯名當時。

translations.literal: Tao distinguished raised hidden bent—searched visited worthy talents—banner summoned thirty-odd persons—all manifest name that time.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Tao elevated the obscure, sought out talent, and summoned over thirty men who soon rose to prominence.

sentences.zh: 人懷慕尚，風俗頗革。

translations.literal: People cherished admiration—customs somewhat reformed.
translations.idiomatic: People admired him and local habits improved.

sentences.zh: 轉北中郎將，督鄴城守事。

translations.literal: Transferred general of the central army on the north—supervised Ye city defense affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He became north army general-in-chief directing Ye's defenses.

sentences.zh: 入為侍中，遷尚書。

translations.literal: Entered as palace attendant—promoted Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as palace attendant and joined the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 以母老辭職，詔曰：「君雖乃心在於色養，然職有上下，旦夕不廢醫藥，且當割情，以隆在公。

translations.literal: Because mother old resigned office—edict said: "Lord although heart is in facial nurturing—yet office has above below—morning evening not abandon medicine—must cut emotion—to elevate in public."
translations.idiomatic: He resigned to care for his aged mother. The edict replied: "Though filial devotion moves you, offices have ranks; attend her with medicine morning and night, yet curb private feeling to serve the state."

sentences.zh: 」濤心求退，表疏數十上，久乃見聽。

translations.literal: Tao heart sought retreat—memorials dozens submitted—long then heard permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Tao still wished to retire and filed dozens of petitions before approval came."

sentences.zh: 除議郎，帝以濤清儉無以供養，特給日契，加賜床帳茵褥。

translations.literal: Appointed gentleman consultant—emperor because Tao pure frugal none to supply nurture—specially gave daily tally—added grant couch curtains cushions.
translations.idiomatic: Named gentleman consultant, he was too poor to support his mother; the emperor granted daily provisions plus couch hangings and bedding."

sentences.zh: 禮秩崇重，時莫為比。

translations.literal: Ritual rank lofty heavy—time none compared.
translations.idiomatic: No contemporary matched the honors paid him."

sentences.zh: 後除太常卿，以疾不就。

translations.literal: Later appointed grand master of ceremonies—because illness did not take.
translations.idiomatic: Offered the court of sacrifices he declined on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 會遭母喪，歸鄉里。

translations.literal: Happened encounter mother's mourning—returned village.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he returned home.

sentences.zh: 濤年逾耳順，居喪過禮，負土成墳，手植松柏。

translations.literal: Tao age passed ear-submit—dwelling mourning exceeded ritual—carried earth completed mound—hand planted pine cypress.
translations.idiomatic: Past sixty, he exceeded mourning propriety—carrying earth for her tomb and planting pines with his own hands.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「吾所共致化者，官人之職是也。

translations.literal: Edict said: "What We together achieve transformation—appointing men's duty is this."
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Ordering appointments is how We transform the realm."

sentences.zh: 方今風欲陵遲，人心進動，宜崇明好惡，鎮以退讓。

translations.literal: Now wind desires decline—people's hearts advance move—should clarify brighten love hate—press with retreat yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Customs slide and ambition runs wild; We must clarify right and wrong and steady men through yielding."

sentences.zh: 山太常雖尚居諒闇，情在難奪，方今務殷，何得遂其志邪！

translations.literal: Grand Master Shan although still dwelling mourning hut—emotion hard seize—now affairs abundant—how obtain fulfill his intent!
translations.idiomatic: Though Minister Shan still mourns and grief grips him, urgent business forbids indulging his wishes!"

sentences.zh: 其以濤為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Cause Tao as minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Appoint Shan Tao minister of Personnel."

sentences.zh: 」濤辭以喪病，章表懇切。

translations.literal: Tao declined citing mourning illness—memorials earnest urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Tao pleaded mourning and illness in earnest memorials."

sentences.zh: 會元皇后崩，遂扶興還洛。

translations.literal: Happened Empress Yuan died—thereupon carried litter returned Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Yuan died he rode the litter back to Luoyang."

sentences.zh: 逼迫詔命，自力就職。

translations.literal: Forced compelled edict orders—self strength took office.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts pressed him until he took office under his own power."

sentences.zh: 前後選舉，周遍內外，而並得其才。

translations.literal: Before after selections—circumscribed inside outside—and together obtained their talents.
translations.idiomatic: His successive selections, reaching every corner of government, matched talent to post."

sentences.zh: 咸甯初，轉太子少傅，加散騎常侍；

translations.literal: Xianning beginning—transferred junior tutor to heir apparent—added cavalier attendant-in-ordinary;
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianning he became junior tutor to the heir with cavalier attendant-in-ordinary;

sentences.zh: 除尚書僕射，加侍中，領吏部。

translations.literal: Appointed vice director Masters of Writing—added palace attendant—supervised Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was named vice director of the Masters of Writing and palace attendant while supervising Personnel.

sentences.zh: 固辭以老疾，上表陳情。

translations.literal: Firmly declined citing old illness—submitted memorial stating feelings.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly pleaded age and illness in memorials.

sentences.zh: 章表數十上，久不攝職，為左丞白褒所奏。

translations.literal: Memorials dozens submitted—long not assumed duties—by assistant director left Bai Bao memorial attacked.
translations.idiomatic: After dozens of memorials he still avoided duties until assistant director Bai Bao impeached him.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「濤以病自聞，但不聽之耳。

translations.literal: Emperor said: "Tao by illness self reported—only not listened to it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Shan Tao reported illness; I simply did not grant leave."

sentences.zh: 使濤坐執銓衡則可，何必上下邪！

translations.literal: Cause Tao sit holding measuring balance then acceptable—why must above below!
translations.idiomatic: Let him oversee appointments seated—why insist he rise for every detail!"

sentences.zh: 不得有所問。

translations.literal: Must not have questioning.
translations.idiomatic: Do not pursue the matter further."

sentences.zh: 」濤不自安，表謝曰：「古之王道，正直而已。

translations.literal: Tao not self secure—memorial thanked saying: "Ancient kingly way—uprightness only."
translations.idiomatic: Uneasy, Shan Tao thanked the throne: "The ancient kings governed through straightforward integrity alone."

sentences.zh: 陛下不可以一老臣為加曲私，臣亦何必屢陳日月。

translations.literal: Your Majesty cannot because one old minister add bent favor—minister also why must repeatedly display sun moon.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty must not bend law for one old minister; neither must I weary you with endless petitions."

sentences.zh: 乞如所表，以章典刑。

translations.literal: Beg as memorialized—to manifest statutes punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Grant my request and uphold the statutes."

sentences.zh: 」帝再手詔曰：「白褒奏君甚妄，所以不即推，直不喜凶赫耳。

translations.literal: Emperor again hand-edicted: "Bai Bao memorialized lord very false—reason not immediately investigate—straight not like fierce glare ear."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote again: "Bai Bao's charge was absurd; I did not investigate only to avoid ugly publicity."

sentences.zh: 君之明度，豈當介意邪！

translations.literal: Lord's bright measure—how should mind boundary!
translations.idiomatic: A man of your discernment should not dwell on it!"

sentences.zh: 便當攝職，令斷章表也。

translations.literal: Then should assume duties—order cut memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Resume your duties and cease these memorials."

sentences.zh: 」濤志必欲退，因發從弟婦喪，輒還外舍。

translations.literal: Tao intent must wish retreat—because issued cousin wife mourning—then returned outer lodging.
translations.idiomatic: Determined to quit, he seized his cousin's wife's funeral as pretext and moved out."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「山僕射近日暫出，遂以微苦未還，豈吾側席之意。

translations.literal: Edict said: "Vice Director Shan recently briefly went out—then because slight ailment not returned—how Our side mat intent!"
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "The vice director left briefly for slight illness and has not returned—is that what I intend by leaving his mat empty?"

sentences.zh: 其遣丞掾奉詔諭旨，若體力故未平康者，便以輿車輿還寺舍。

translations.literal: Cause send assistant clerk carry edict declare intent—if strength originally not peaceful healthy—then use litter cart lift return monastery lodging.
translations.idiomatic: Send clerks with my words: if he remains unwell, carry him back to office in a litter."

sentences.zh: 」濤辭不獲已，乃起視事。

translations.literal: Tao declined not obtain stop—then rose attended affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to refuse further, he returned to duty."

sentences.zh: 濤再居選職十有餘年，每一官缺，輒啟擬數人，詔旨有所向，然後顯奏，隨帝意所欲為先。

translations.literal: Tao again dwelt selection office ten-odd years—each one office vacancy—then proposed several persons—edict intent had direction—then manifest memorial—follow emperor intent what desired as first.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Tao directed personnel for over a decade; for each vacancy he proposed several names, learned the emperor's preference, then formally recommended whoever the emperor favored first.

sentences.zh: 故帝之所用，或非舉首，眾情不察，以濤輕重任意。

translations.literal: Therefore emperor's employed—perhaps not recommendation head—multitude feeling not perceive—thought Tao light heavy arbitrary.
translations.idiomatic: Appointments sometimes skipped Shan Tao's top pick; unaware critics accused him of arbitrary favoritism.

sentences.zh: 或譖之於帝，故帝手詔戒濤曰：「夫用人惟才，不遺疏遠單賤，天下便化矣。

translations.literal: Some slandered him to emperor—therefore emperor hand-edict warned Tao: "Employing men only talent—not abandon distant humble poor—realm then transforms."
translations.idiomatic: Slander reached the emperor, who wrote: "Employ men on merit alone, ignoring humble origins, and the realm will follow."

sentences.zh: 」而濤行之自若，一年之後眾情乃寢。

translations.literal: Yet Tao practiced self like so—one year after multitude feeling then rested.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Tao continued unchanged; within a year the gossip died."

sentences.zh: 濤所奏甄拔人物，各為題目，時稱《山公啟事》。

translations.literal: What Tao memorialized distinguishing raising persons—each made titles—time called Lord Shan's Memorial Notices.
translations.idiomatic: His nomination memorials, each headed by topic, became known as "Lord Shan's Official Posts."

sentences.zh: 濤中立於朝，晚值後黨專權，不欲任楊氏，多有諷諫，帝雖悟而不能改。

translations.literal: Tao neutral stood at court—late met empress faction monopolize power—not wished employ Yang clan—much indirect remonstrance—emperor although understood yet could not change.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Tao stayed neutral; late in life the empress's faction dominated and he resisted empowering the Yangs, often remonstrating—the emperor understood yet could not change course.

sentences.zh: 後以年衰疾篤，上疏告退曰：「臣年垂八十，救命旦夕，若有毫末之益，豈遺力于聖時，迫以老耄，不復任事。

translations.literal: Later because age decline illness severe—submitted memorial announcing retreat saying: "Minister age nears eighty—life-order dawn dusk—if there be hair-tip benefit—how abandon strength in sage time—forced by aged decrepit—no longer bear affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Age and grave illness moved him to resign: "Near eighty, I await death daily; were any strength left I would spare none for your reign, but senility bars further service."

sentences.zh: 今四海休息，天下思化，從而靜之，百姓自正。

translations.literal: Now four seas rest—realm desires transformation—following thereby quiet it—hundred surnames self correct.
translations.idiomatic: The realm rests; people crave moral sway—calm them and commoners order themselves."

sentences.zh: 但當崇風尚教以敦之耳，陛下亦復何事。

translations.literal: Only should honor wind esteem teaching to urge it ear—Your Majesty also again what affair.
translations.idiomatic: You need only champion teaching by example—little else remains for Your Majesty to do."

sentences.zh: 臣耳目聾瞑，不能自勵。

translations.literal: Minister ears eyes deaf dim—cannot self exert.
translations.idiomatic: My eyes and ears fail—I cannot rouse myself."

sentences.zh: 君臣父子，其間無文，是以直陳愚情，乞聽所請。

translations.literal: Lord minister father son—between them no pattern—therefore straight display foolish feeling—beg hear request.
translations.idiomatic: Between lord and minister, father and son, ritual yields to truth—I speak plainly and beg consent."

sentences.zh: 」乃免冠徒跣，上還印綬。

translations.literal: Then removed cap barefoot—submitted return seals ribbons.
translations.idiomatic: He doffed cap and shoes and returned his seals."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「天下事廣，加吳土初平，凡百草創，當共盡意化之。

translations.literal: Edict said: "Realm affairs broad—add Wu soil first pacified—everything hundred grass origins—should together exhaust intent transform them."
translations.idiomatic: The edict answered: "Affairs are vast and Wu newly pacified; everything must be built—we must labor together to civilize it."

sentences.zh: 君不深識往心而以小疾求退，豈所望於君邪！

translations.literal: Lord not deeply recognize former heart yet by small ailment seek retreat—how hoped from lord!
translations.idiomatic: You ignore my earlier intent and plead minor illness—is that what I expect of you!"

sentences.zh: 朕猶側席，未得垂拱，君亦何得高尚其事乎！

translations.literal: We still side mat—not obtained hands-fold—lord also how obtain lofty that affair!
translations.idiomatic: I still leave your mat empty—I cannot rule effortlessly—how may you pose as lofty recluse!"

sentences.zh: 當崇至公，勿復為虛飾之煩。

translations.literal: Should honor utmost public—do not again vain ornament's bother.
translations.idiomatic: Serve the greater good and spare Us hollow gestures."

sentences.zh: 」濤苦表請退，詔又不許。

translations.literal: Tao bitterly memorial begged retreat—edict again not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: His bitter pleas again failed."

sentences.zh: 尚書令衛瓘奏：「濤以微苦，久不視職。

translations.literal: Director of Masters of Writing Wei Guan memorialized: "Tao because slight ailment long not attended duties."
translations.idiomatic: Director Wei Guan reported: "Shan Tao cites minor illness and long neglects duty."

sentences.zh: 手詔頻煩，猶未順旨。

translations.literal: Hand edicts came frequent and pressing—still he did not comply with the intent.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial rescripts arrived again and again, yet he still refused to obey.

sentences.zh: 參議以為無專節之尚，違在公之義。

translations.literal: The counselors deemed he lacked the esteem accorded to singular integrity and violated the righteousness due in public office.
translations.idiomatic: The advisory officials argued that he fell short of the virtue singled out for honor and betrayed the duty of impartial service to the state.

sentences.zh: 若實沈篤，亦不宜居位。

translations.literal: If truly sunk gravely ill, also not suitable to occupy the position.
translations.idiomatic: Even if he were genuinely and gravely ill, he should still not hold office.

sentences.zh: 可免濤官。

translations.literal: May dismiss Tao from office.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Tao should be removed from his post.

sentences.zh: 」中詔瓘曰：「濤以德素為朝之望，而常深退讓，至於懇切。

translations.literal: " An interim edict told Wei Guan: "Tao by plain virtue is the court's hope—yet constantly deeply yields and withdraws—to the point of earnestness.
translations.idiomatic: " …" An interim edict instructed Wei Guan: "Shan Tao is esteemed for his plain virtue and is the mainstay of the court, yet he constantly insists on retiring—most earnestly so.

sentences.zh: 故比有詔，欲必奪其志，以匡輔不逮。

translations.literal: Therefore recently there have been edicts—wishing necessarily to seize away his resolve—to rectify and aid where I fall short.
translations.idiomatic: Hence repeated edicts have sought to override his determination so that he may assist me where my abilities do not reach.

sentences.zh: 主者既不思明詔旨，而反深加詆案。

translations.literal: Those in charge already did not ponder the bright intent of the edicts—yet on the contrary deeply added slander and case-making.
translations.idiomatic: Those responsible have ignored the clear meaning of the edicts and instead piled accusations on him.

sentences.zh: 虧崇賢之風，以重吾不德，何以示遠近邪！

translations.literal: It defeats the wind of esteeming worthies—to double my lacking virtue—how show far and near!
translations.idiomatic: This undermines the spirit of honoring the worthy and compounds my lack of virtue—how am I to show myself to the realm!

sentences.zh: 」濤不得已，又起視事。

translations.literal: " Tao had no choice—again rose and attended to affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Left no choice, Shan Tao resumed his duties.

sentences.zh: 太康初，遷右僕射，加光祿大夫，侍中、掌選如故。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taikang—promoted Right Vice Director—added Grand Master of Splendid Carriage—attendant-in-ordinary and superintending selection as before.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taikang era he was promoted to Right Vice Director and granted the title Grand Master of Splendid Carriage; he remained attendant-in-ordinary and in charge of appointments as before.

sentences.zh: 濤以老疾固辭，手詔曰：「君以道德為世模表，況自先帝識君遠意。

translations.literal: Tao citing old age and illness firmly declined—a handwritten edict said: "You by dao and virtue are the age's model pattern—moreover since the former emperor knew your far intent.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Tao firmly resigned on grounds of age and infirmity; a handwritten edict replied: "You exemplify moral excellence for the world, and the late emperor already grasped your long-term aims.

sentences.zh: 吾將倚君以穆風俗，何乃欲舍遠朝政，獨高其志耶！

translations.literal: I will rely on you to harmonize customs—how then wish to cast away and distance court governance—alone elevate your resolve!
translations.idiomatic: I depend on you to bring harmony to customs—why would you abandon court affairs and pride yourself on lofty withdrawal?

sentences.zh: 吾之至懷故不足以喻乎，何來言至懇切也。

translations.literal: My utmost regard thus insufficient to make understood—why come words utmost earnest.
translations.idiomatic: Surely my deepest regard cannot be put across—why do you speak with such desperate earnestness?

sentences.zh: 且當以時自力，深副至望。

translations.literal: Moreover ought by the times exert yourself—deeply match utmost hope.
translations.idiomatic: You must meantime rally your strength and fully live up to what I expect of you.

sentences.zh: 君不降志，朕不安席。

translations.literal: If you do not lower your resolve—I am not secure on the mat.
translations.idiomatic: Unless you set aside this resolve, I cannot rest easy.

sentences.zh: 」濤又上表固讓，不許。

translations.literal: " Tao again submitted a memorial firmly declining—not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Tao submitted another memorial firmly declining; permission was refused.

sentences.zh: 吳平之後，帝詔天下罷軍役，示海內大安，州郡悉去兵，大郡置武吏百人，小郡五十人。

translations.literal: After Wu was pacified—the emperor edicted the realm to abolish military service—to show within the seas great peace—provinces and commanderies all removed troops—great commanderies placed martial clerks hundred persons—small commanderies fifty.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu fell, the emperor ordered the empire to stand down levies and signals that all within the seas were at peace; provinces and commanderies stripped their garrisons—larger commanderies kept a hundred military clerks, smaller ones fifty.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗講武于宣武場，濤時有疾，詔乘步輦從。

translations.literal: The emperor once lectured martial at Xuanwu Field—Tao at the time had illness—edicted to ride a litter and follow.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor once held military exercises at Xuanwu Field, Shan Tao was ill and was ordered to follow in a sedan chair.

sentences.zh: 因與盧欽論用兵之本，以為不宜去州郡武備，其論甚精。

translations.literal: Thereupon with Lu Qin discussed the root of using troops—deemed not suitable to remove province-commandery martial preparedness—his discourse very refined.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Tao then discussed the fundamentals of warfare with Lu Qin and argued that local military readiness should not be dismantled; his reasoning was acute.

sentences.zh: 于時咸以濤不學孫、吳，而暗與之合。

translations.literal: At the time all thought Tao did not study Sun and Wu—yet darkly with them agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone assumed Shan Tao had not studied Sunzi and Wuzi, yet his views tacitly matched theirs.

sentences.zh: 帝稱之曰：「天下名言也。

translations.literal: The emperor praised it saying: "Under-heaven famous saying.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor declared, "That is a maxim for the whole realm."

sentences.zh: 」而不能用。

translations.literal: " Yet could not use.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he did not put it into practice.

sentences.zh: 及永寧之後，屢有變難，寇賊猋起，郡國皆以無備不能制，天下遂以大亂，如濤言焉。

translations.literal: When after Yongning—repeatedly there were changes and disasters—bandits and thieves whirlwind rose—commanderies and principalities all because no preparedness could not control—under-heaven thereupon by great chaos—as Tao had spoken.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yongning era, turmoil broke out again and again; bandits sprang up like a whirlwind, and provinces could not cope through lack of preparation—the realm descended into great chaos, just as Shan Tao had warned.

sentences.zh: 後拜司徒，濤復固讓。

translations.literal: Later appointed Minister of Education—Tao again firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Minister of Education; Shan Tao again firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「郡年耆德茂，朝之碩老，是以授君台輔之位。

translations.literal: " Edict said: "Commandery years aged virtue lush—court's great elder—therefore grant you terrace-assist position.
translations.idiomatic: " …" The edict read: "You are advanced in years and rich in virtue—the seniormost elder of the court—and therefore we confer on you a seat among the highest ministers.

sentences.zh: 而遠崇克讓，至於反覆，良用於邑。

translations.literal: Yet afar esteem able yield—arriving at back-and-forth—truly use yuyi sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you insist from afar on humble refusal to the point of repetition—I am deeply pained.

sentences.zh: 君當終始朝政，翼輔朕躬。

translations.literal: You ought end-to-begin court governance—wing-assist my person.
translations.idiomatic: You must see court affairs through from beginning to end and support me as my wing and aide.

sentences.zh: 」濤又表曰：「臣事天朝三十餘年，卒無毫釐以崇大化。

translations.literal: " Tao again memorial said: "Your servant serves the celestial court thirty some years—finally no hair-tip to exalt great transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Tao submitted another memorial: "I have served the dynasty for more than thirty years and have not advanced the great civilizing work by the slightest measure.

sentences.zh: 陛下私臣無已，猥授三司。

translations.literal: Your Majesty favors your servant without end—rudely grants the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty showers favor on me without limit and has undeservedly placed me among the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 臣聞德薄位高，力少任重，上有折足之凶，下有廟門之咎，願陛下垂累世之恩，乞臣骸骨。

translations.literal: Your servant hears virtue thin position high—strength little burden heavy—above has broken-foot ill omen—below has temple-gate blame—wish Your Majesty extend accumulated-worlds grace—beg servant's bones.
translations.idiomatic: They say thin virtue with high rank and little strength with heavy duty brings the omen of a broken tripod leg and blame at the ancestral gate—I beg Your Majesty, in kindness accumulated over generations, to let me retire my bones.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「君翼贊朝政，保乂皇家，匡佐之勳，朕所倚賴。

translations.literal: Edict said: "You wing-assist court governance—protect the royal house—the merit of rectifying aid—I rely on.
translations.idiomatic: The edict replied: "You steady the court, safeguard the house of Jin, and your service as pillar is what I depend on.

sentences.zh: 司徒之職，實掌幫教，故用敬授，以答群望。

translations.literal: The Minister of Education's duty—indeed manages assist-teaching—therefore use respectful grant—to answer crowd hope.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Education truly oversees moral instruction; this appointment honors you and answers what everyone expects.

sentences.zh: 豈宜沖讓以自抑損邪！

translations.literal: How suitable humble yield to self suppress diminish!
translations.idiomatic: How can it be right to yield in modesty and sell yourself short?

sentences.zh: 」已敕斷章表，使者乃臥加章綬。

translations.literal: " Already ordered stop memorials—envoy then while lying applied seal and cords.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials had already been ordered stopped; the envoy then placed the seal and ribbons on him while he lay abed.

sentences.zh: 濤曰：「垂沒之人，豈可汙官府乎！

translations.literal: Tao said: "About-to-drown person—how can defile official offices!
translations.idiomatic: Shan Tao said, "A dying man cannot soil the offices of government!"

sentences.zh: 」輿疾歸家。

translations.literal: " By litter illness returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He was carried home ill.

sentences.zh: 乙薨，時年七十九，詔賜東園秘器、朝服一具、衣一襲、錢五十萬、布百匹，以供喪事，策贈司徒，蜜印紫綬，侍中貂蟬，新遝伯蜜印青硃綬，祭乙太牢，諡曰康。

translations.literal: Yi died—at the time age seventy-nine—edict granted eastern park secret vessels—court robe one set—garments one suit—cash fifty myriad—cloth hundred bolts—to supply funeral affairs—document posthumously gifted Minister of Education—seal with honey purple cords—attendant-in-ordinary sable tails—Xinta baron seal honey blue-vermilion cords—sacrifice Yi grand beast—posthumous title said Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Tao died at seventy-nine. The court granted burial gifts from the imperial workshop, a court robe, a suit of clothes, five hundred thousand cash, and a hundred bolts of cloth for the funeral; he was posthumously honored as Minister of Education with the seal and purple ribbons of that office, the regalia of attendant-in-ordinary, and the barony seal of Xinta with blue and vermilion ribbons; a grand sacrifice was offered, and his posthumous name was Kang.

sentences.zh: 將葬，賜錢四十萬、布百匹。

translations.literal: About to bury—granted cash forty myriad—cloth hundred bolts.
translations.idiomatic: When the burial approached, the court granted another four hundred thousand cash and a hundred bolts of cloth.

sentences.zh: 左長史範晷等上言：「濤舊第屋十間，子孫不相容。

translations.literal: Left chief clerk Fan Gui etc. upward spoke: "Tao old mansion rooms ten—sons grandsons not mutually accommodate.
translations.idiomatic: Left chief clerk Fan Gui and others reported: "Shan Tao's former house has only ten rooms; his children and grandchildren cannot fit."

sentences.zh: 」帝為之立室。

translations.literal: " The emperor for him built chambers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had a residence built for them.

sentences.zh: 初，濤布衣家貧，謂妻韓氏曰：「忍饑寒，我後當作三公，但不知卿堪公夫人不耳！

translations.literal: Initially Tao cloth-clothes family poor—said to wife Lady Han: "Endure hunger cold—I later shall become Three Dukes—but not know if you can bear duchess or not!
translations.idiomatic: Long ago, when Shan Tao was a commoner and poor, he told his wife Lady Han, "Bear with hunger and cold—I will rise to the Three Dukes one day; only I do not know whether you can be a duchess!"

sentences.zh: 」及居榮貴，貞慎儉約，雖爵同千乘，而無嬪媵。

translations.literal: " When dwelt glory noble—chaste cautious frugal—although noble rank equal thousand chariots—yet without concubines.
translations.idiomatic: Once he enjoyed honor and wealth, he remained chaste, careful, and frugal; though his rank matched that of a lord of a thousand chariots, he kept no concubines.

sentences.zh: 祿賜俸秩，散之親故。

translations.literal: Salary grants stipend ranks—dispersed them kin old-friends.
translations.idiomatic: He distributed salaries, gifts, and stipends among kinsmen and old friends.

sentences.zh: 初，陳郡袁毅嘗為鬲令，貪濁而賂遺公卿，以求虛譽，亦遺濤絲百斤，濤不欲異于時，受而藏於閣上。

translations.literal: Initially Chen commandery Yuan Yi once was Ge county magistrate—greedy turbid and bribed gifted dukes ministers—to seek empty fame—also gifted Tao silk hundred jin—Tao not wished differ from times—accepted and hid on loft.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yuan Yi of Chen commandery, as magistrate of Ge, was corrupt and sent bribes to high officials to win hollow praise; he also sent Shan Tao a hundred jin of silk. Shan Tao did not wish to seem out of step with his contemporaries, so he accepted it and stowed it in his loft.

sentences.zh: 後毅事露，檻車送廷尉，凡所以賂，皆見推檢。

translations.literal: Later Yi's affair exposed—cage-cart sent to Minister of Justice—all whereby bribed—all seen pushed examined.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Yi's crimes came to light, he was carted to the Minister of Justice, and every bribe was traced and investigated.

sentences.zh: 濤乃取絲付吏，積年塵埃，印封如初。

translations.literal: Tao then took silk give clerk—accumulated years dust—seal stamp as first.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Tao then handed the silk to the clerks; years of dust lay on it, and the seals were intact as on the day they arrived.

sentences.zh: 濤飲酒至八斗方醉，帝欲試之，乃以酒八斗飲濤，而密益其酒，濤極本量而止。

translations.literal: Tao drank wine to eight dou then drunk—emperor wished test him—thereupon with wine eight dou made Tao drink—yet secretly increased his wine—Tao reached original measure then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Tao could drink eight dou of wine before becoming drunk. The emperor wished to test him and gave him eight dou—but secretly added more. Shan Tao stopped when he reached his natural limit.

sentences.zh: 有五子：該、淳、允、謨、簡。

translations.literal: Had five sons: Gai, Chun, Yun, Mo, Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons: Gai, Chun, Yun, Mo, and Jian.

sentences.zh: 該字伯倫，嗣父爵，仕至并州刺史、太子左率，贈長水校尉。

translations.literal: Gai courtesy name Bolun—inherited father noble—served to Bingzhou regional inspector—Crown Prince left commandant—posthumously awarded Chief of Changshui.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Gai, courtesy name Bolun, inherited his father's noble rank and rose to regional inspector of Bingzhou and left commandant to the crown prince; posthumously he was awarded chief of Changshui.

sentences.zh: 該子瑋字彥祖，翊軍校尉，次子世回，吏部郎、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Gai's son Wei courtesy name Yanzu—Colonel Who Assists the Army—second son Shihui—Ministry of Personnel gentleman—regular attendant on palace affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Gai's son Shan Wei, courtesy name Yanzu, was Colonel Who Assists the Army; his second son, Shihui, served as a gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel and regular attendant on palace affairs.

sentences.zh: 淳字子玄，不仕，允字叔真，奉車都尉，並少尪病，形甚短小，而聰敏過人。

translations.literal: Chun courtesy name Zixuan—not served—Yun courtesy name Shuzhen—commandant of chariots—both youth weak illness—form very short small—yet clever keen surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Chun, courtesy name Zixuan, did not take office. Shan Yun, courtesy name Shuzhen, was commandant of the imperial chariots. Both were frail and sickly from youth, very short in stature, yet clever beyond ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 武帝聞而欲見之，濤不敢辭，以問於允。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu heard and wished see them—Tao not dared decline—thereby asked Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu heard of them and wished to meet them; Shan Tao did not dare refuse and put the question to Shan Yun.

sentences.zh: 允自以尪陋，不肯行。

translations.literal: Yun himself thought weak ugly—not willing go.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Yun considered himself too frail and unsightly to go.

sentences.zh: 濤以為勝己，乃表曰：「臣二子尪病，宜絕人事，不敢受詔。」

translations.literal: Tao thought surpassed self—thereupon memorial said: "Your servant two sons weak ill—ought cut off human affairs—not dare accept edict."
translations.idiomatic: Shan Tao felt Yun surpassed himself and therefore memorialized: "My two sons are chronically ill and ought to be cut off from worldly affairs; I dare not accept the summons."

sentences.zh: 謨字季長，明惠有才智，官至司空掾。

translations.literal: Mo courtesy name Jichang—bright keen had talent wisdom—office reached Minister of Works aide.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Mo, courtesy name Jichang, was bright, keen, and talented; he rose to aide in the Minister of Works bureau.

translations.literal: The manuscript gives only the equals sign, likely a section marker.
translations.idiomatic: The received text marks a break here with an equals sign alone.

sentences.zh: 子簡

translations.literal: Son Jian.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Shan Jian.

sentences.zh: =簡字季倫。

translations.literal: = Jian's courtesy name was Jilun.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Jian, courtesy name Jilun.

sentences.zh: 性溫雅，有父風，年二十餘，濤不之知也。

translations.literal: Nature mild elegant—had father's manner—age twenty some—Tao not him knew.
translations.idiomatic: He was mild and refined and took after his father, yet past twenty his father still did not recognize his quality.

sentences.zh: 簡歎曰：「吾年幾三十，而不為家公所知！

translations.literal: Jian sighed saying: "My age nearly thirty—yet not by house elder known!
translations.idiomatic: Shan Jian sighed, "I am almost thirty, and my father still does not know me!"

sentences.zh: 」後與譙國嵇紹、沛郡劉謨、弘農楊准齊名。

translations.literal: " Later with Qiao principality Xi Shao—Pei commandery Liu Mo—Hongnong Yang Zhun same fame.
translations.idiomatic: Later he ranked with Xi Shao of Qiao, Liu Mo of Pei, and Yang Zhun of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 初為太子舍人，累遷太子庶子、黃門郎，出為青州刺史。

translations.literal: First was Crown Prince attendant—accumulated promoted Crown Prince junior mentor—gentleman at yellow gate—went out as Qingzhou regional inspector.
translations.idiomatic: He began as attendant to the crown prince, rose through junior mentor to the heir and gentleman at the Yellow Gate, then left the capital as regional inspector of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 徵拜侍中，頃之，轉尚書。

translations.literal: Summoned appointed attendant-in-ordinary—shortly—transferred to Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed attendant-in-ordinary; soon afterward he moved to the Ministry.

sentences.zh: 曆鎮軍將軍、荊州刺史，領南蠻校尉，不行，復拜尚書。

translations.literal: Passed General Who Garrisons the Army—Jingzhou regional inspector—concurrently Colonel of Southern Man—not took post—again appointed Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He served as General Who Garrisons the Army and regional inspector of Jingzhou and held the concurrent title Colonel of the Southern Man but did not take up the post; he was again appointed to the Ministry.

sentences.zh: 光熙初，轉吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Guangxi beginning—transferred Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guangxi era he became Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 永嘉初，出為雍州刺史、鎮西將軍。

translations.literal: Yongjia beginning—went out as Yongzhou regional inspector—General Who Guards the West.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongjia era he went out as regional inspector of Yongzhou and General Who Guards the West.

sentences.zh: 徵為尚書左僕射，領吏部。

translations.literal: Summoned as Left Vice Director of Ministers—concurrently Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel and headed that bureau.

sentences.zh: 簡欲令朝臣各舉所知，以廣得才之路。

translations.literal: Jian wished make court ministers each recommend those known—to broaden obtain talent road.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Jian wished court officials each to recommend men they knew so as to widen the path to finding talent.

sentences.zh: 上疏曰：「臣以為自古興替，實在官人；

translations.literal: Submitted memorial said: "Your servant thinks from ancient rise-decline—indeed lies in appointing men;
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial: "I hold that rise and fall since antiquity truly hinge on the appointment of officials;

sentences.zh: 苟得其才，則無物不理。

translations.literal: If obtain their talents—then nothing not regulated.
translations.idiomatic: if the right men are chosen, nothing will go untended.

sentences.zh: 《書》言：'知人則哲，惟帝難之。

translations.literal: Documents says: 'Know men then wise—only emperor difficult it.

translations.idiomatic: The people of Jingzhou were pleased and submitted.

translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 」帝雖以是言釋之，然為清慎者所鄙，由是損名。

translations.idiomatic: Although the emperor thus excused him, men who prized purity despised him, and his reputation suffered.

translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong showed no outstanding talent in office, yet routine administration stayed in good order.

translations.idiomatic: He later rose to Supernumerary Grand Master and Minister of Personnel, then left office for his mother's mourning.

translations.idiomatic: He was deeply filial yet ignored ritual propriety: he drank and ate meat and sometimes watched weiqi, yet his looks wasted away until he needed a staff to rise.

sentences.zh: 」時和嶠亦居父喪，以禮法自持，量米而食，哀毀不逾於戎。

translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Liu Yi, "He Qiao's exhaustion exceeds the rites and worries me."

sentences.zh: 」毅曰：「嶠雖寢苫食粥，乃生孝耳。

translations.literal: " Yi said: "Qiao although slept straw ate gruel—only living filial ear.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi replied, "He Qiao sleeps on straw and eats gruel—that is the filial piety of the living.

sentences.zh: 至於王戎，所謂死孝，陛下當先憂之。

translations.idiomatic: As for Wang Rong, this is filial grief unto death—Your Majesty should worry for him first."

sentences.zh: 」戎先有吐疾，居喪增甚。

translations.literal: " Rong before had vomiting illness—mourning increased severe.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong had long suffered vomiting; mourning made it far worse.

translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent physicians and medicines and barred visitors.

translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jun dominated the government, Wang Rong was appointed grand tutor to the crown prince.

translations.idiomatic: After Yang Jun was executed, Duke Sima Yao of Dong'an monopolized punishments and rewards and awed court and countryside.

sentences.zh: 」繇不從，果得罪。

sentences.zh: 及石勒、王彌寇京師，以衍都督征討諸軍事、持節、假黃鉞以距之。

translations.literal: When Shi Le Wang Mi raid capital—appointed Yan area commander campaign affairs—hold credentials—borrow yellow axe to resist.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Le and Wang Mi threatened Luoyang, Wang Yan was named area commander for punitive campaigns with full credentials and ceremonial axe to oppose them.

sentences.zh: 衍使前將軍曹武、左衛將軍王景等擊賊，退之，獲其輜重。

translations.literal: Yan sent forward general Cao Wu—left guard general Wang Jing etc. strike bandits—repelled them—obtained their baggage.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan sent Forward General Cao Wu and Left Guard Wang Jing against the raiders, drove them back, and captured their baggage train.

sentences.zh: 遷太尉，尚書令如故。

translations.literal: Promoted Grand Commandant—Minister Head as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Commandant while remaining Minister Head.

sentences.zh: 封武陵侯，辭封不受。

translations.literal: Enfeoffed Wuling marquis—declined enfeoffment not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed marquis of Wuling but declined the patent.

sentences.zh: 時洛陽危逼，多欲遷都以避其難，而衍獨賣車牛以安眾心。

translations.literal: At time Luoyang peril pressed—many wished move capital to escape hardship—yet Yan alone sold carts oxen to calm crowd hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang was under siege and many wished to move the capital; Wang Yan alone sold carts and oxes to steady morale.

sentences.zh: 越之討苟晞也，衍以太尉為太傅軍司。

translations.literal: Yue's campaign Gou Xi—Yan by Grand Commandant as Grand Tutor army director.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue campaigned against Gou Xi, Wang Yan served as army director to the grand tutor as Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 及越薨，眾共推為元帥。

translations.literal: When Yue died—crowd together pushed as supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: After Yue died the host wished to make Wang Yan supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 衍以賊寇鋒起，懼不敢當。

translations.literal: Yan because bandit raiders spear rose—feared not dare accept.
translations.idiomatic: Raiders sprang up on every side and Wang Yan feared to accept command.

sentences.zh: 辭曰：「吾少無宦情，隨牒推移，遂至於此。

translations.literal: Declined saying: "I youth no office feeling—follow dispatch shift—thereupon arrived here.
translations.idiomatic: He declined: "I never burned for office; I drifted with appointments until I landed here.

sentences.zh: 今日之事，安可以非才處之。

translations.literal: Today's affairs—how can by non-talent handle.
translations.idiomatic: Today's crisis is no place for an untalented man."

sentences.zh: 」俄而舉軍為石勒所破，勒呼王公，與之相見，問衍以晉故。

translations.literal: " Shortly whole army by Shi Le broken—Le summoned kings dukes—with him met—asked Yan by Jin former.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the whole army fell to Shi Le; Le summoned the great lords to meet him and questioned Wang Yan about Jin's decline.

sentences.zh: 衍為陳禍敗之由，雲計不在己。

translations.literal: Yan for presented disaster defeat's cause—said plan not in self.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan laid out why calamity came and said the designs were not his own.

sentences.zh: 勒甚悅之，與語移日。

translations.literal: Le very pleased him—with words moved sun.
translations.idiomatic: Le was pleased and talked with him from dawn to dusk.

sentences.zh: 衍自說少不豫事，欲求自免，因勸勒稱尊號。

translations.literal: Yan self said youth not participate affairs—wished seek self exempt—thereupon urged Le assume honored title.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan insisted he had never meddled in policy and begged to live; he urged Le to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 勒怒曰：「君名蓋四海，身居重任，少壯登朝，至於白首，何得言不豫世事邪！

translations.literal: Le angrily said: "Your name covers four seas—body dwells heavy post—young strong ascended court—arriving white head—how get say not participate world affairs!
translations.idiomatic: Le snarled, "Your fame fills the realm; you bear heavy office from youth to white hair—how dare you say you took no part in affairs!"

sentences.zh: 破壞天下，正是君罪。

translations.literal: Destroy under-heaven—just is your crime.
translations.idiomatic: Ruining the empire is your crime."

sentences.zh: 」使左右扶出。

translations.literal: " Ordered attendants support out.
translations.idiomatic: He had attendants lead Wang Yan away.

sentences.zh: 謂其党孔萇曰：「吾行天下多矣，未嘗見如此人，當可活不？

translations.literal: Told his faction Kong Chang: "I travel under-heaven much—never seen such person—ought can live not?
translations.idiomatic: He said to his follower Kong Chang, "I have traveled the realm—never seen such a man—should he live?"

sentences.zh: 」萇曰：「彼晉之三公，必不為我盡力，又何足貴乎！

translations.literal: " Chang said: "That Jin's Three Dukes—surely not for me exert strength—again what worth honor!
translations.idiomatic: Kong Chang replied, "Those Jin Three Dukes will never serve us—why spare him?"

sentences.zh: 」勒曰：「要不可加以鋒刃也。

translations.literal: " Le said: "Essential cannot add upon blade edge.
translations.idiomatic: Le said, "Still, we must not run him through."

sentences.zh: 」使人夜排牆填殺之。

translations.literal: " Sent person night push wall fill kill him.
translations.idiomatic: That night he had men push a wall over him and crush him to death.

sentences.zh: 衍將死，顧而言曰：「嗚呼！

translations.literal: Yan about die—turned and said: "Alas!
translations.idiomatic: As he faced death Wang Yan turned and cried, "Alas!

sentences.zh: 吾曹雖不如古人，向若不祖尚浮虛，戮力以匡天下，猶可不至今日。

translations.literal: We band although not equal ancients—if earlier had not revered float void—joined strength to rectify under-heaven—still could not arrive today.
translations.idiomatic: We may fall short of the ancients, yet had we not honored hollow vanity and had joined to save the realm, we might not have come to this."

sentences.zh: 」時年五十六。

translations.literal: " At time age fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 衍俊秀有令望，希心玄遠，未嘗語利。

translations.literal: Yan handsome elegant had fair fame—hope heart dark far—never spoke profit.
translations.idiomatic: Handsome and esteemed, Wang Yan aspired to the transcendent and never spoke of gain.

sentences.zh: 王敦過江，常稱之曰：「夷甫處眾中，如珠玉在瓦石間。

translations.literal: Wang Dun crossed river—often praised saying: "Yifu dwells crowd middle—like pearls jade among tiles stones.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Dun crossed south he often said, "Yifu among the crowd is pearls and jade among tiles and stone."

sentences.zh: 」顧愷之作畫贊，亦稱衍岩岩清峙，壁立千仞。

translations.literal: " Gu Kaizhi made portrait praise—also praised Yan rocky-rocky clear stand—cliff stand thousand ren.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Kaizhi's portrait encomium likewise praised Wang Yan as sheer cliffs rising a thousand ren.

sentences.zh: 其為人所尚如此。

translations.literal: He by people esteemed thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem he commanded.

sentences.zh: 子玄，字眉子，少慕簡曠，亦有俊才，與衛玠齊名。

translations.literal: Son Xuan courtesy name Meizi—youth admired simple vast—also had handsome talent—with Wei Jie same fame.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wang Xuan, courtesy name Meizi, loved simplicity and freedom in youth and had rare talent; he ranked with Wei Jie.

sentences.zh: 荀籓用為陳留太守，屯尉氏。

translations.literal: Xun Fan employed Chenliu grand warden—garrison Weishi.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Fan appointed him grand warden of Chenliu, stationed at Weishi.

sentences.zh: 玄素名家，有豪氣，荒弊之時，人情不附，將赴祖逖，為盜所害焉。

translations.literal: Xuan plain famous house—had heroic spirit—waste ruin time—human hearts not attach—about go Zu Ti—by bandits harmed.
translations.idiomatic: Of eminent stock and bold temper, in those ruined times support fled; headed to join Zu Ti he was killed by bandits.

translations.literal: The manuscript gives only the equals sign, likely a section marker.
translations.idiomatic: The received text marks a break here with an equals sign alone.

sentences.zh: 衍弟澄

translations.literal: Yan's younger brother Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: His brother was Wang Cheng.

sentences.zh: =澄字平子。

translations.literal: = Cheng courtesy name Pingzi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Cheng, courtesy name Pingzi.

sentences.zh: 生而警悟，雖未能言，見人舉動，便識其意。

translations.literal: Born alert awaken—although not yet speak—saw person movements—then knew intent.
translations.idiomatic: Alert from birth, before he could speak he read people's movements and grasped their intent.

sentences.zh: 衍妻郭性貪鄙，欲令婢路上擔糞。

translations.literal: Yan wife Guo nature greedy vulgar—wished order maidservants road above carry dung.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan's wife Guo was greedy and base; she wanted maids to haul dung along the road.

sentences.zh: 澄年十四，諫郭以為不可。

translations.literal: Cheng age fourteen—remonstrated Guo thought not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen Wang Cheng remonstrated with Lady Guo that it would not do.

sentences.zh: 郭大怒，謂澄曰：「昔夫人臨終，以小郎屬新婦，不以新婦屬小郎。

translations.literal: Guo greatly angry—told Cheng: "Former madame faced end—by young lord entrusted new bride—not by new bride entrust young lord.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Guo raged and told him, "When your mother lay dying she entrusted you to me—not me to you."

sentences.zh: 」因捉其衣裾，將杖之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon seized his garment skirt—about cane him.
translations.idiomatic: She seized his robe and meant to beat him.

sentences.zh: 澄爭得脫，逾窗而走。

translations.literal: Cheng struggled obtained escape—leaped window and ran.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Cheng broke free and fled out the window.

sentences.zh: 衍有重名于世，時人許以人倫之鑒。

translations.literal: Yan had heavy fame in age—time people granted human-relations discernment.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan enjoyed towering fame; contemporaries acknowledged him as judge of character.

sentences.zh: 尤重澄及王敦、庾敳，嘗為天下人士目曰：「阿平第一，子嵩第二，處仲第三。

translations.literal: Especially valued Cheng and Wang Dun Yu Kai—once for under-heaven gentlemen eyed: "A-Ping first—Zisong second—Zhongzhong third.
translations.idiomatic: He prized Wang Cheng, Wang Dun, and Yu Kai above all; he once ranked notables: "A-Ping first, Zisong second, Zhongzhong third."

sentences.zh: 」澄嘗謂衍曰：「兄形似道，而神鋒太俊。

translations.literal: " Cheng once told Yan: "Elder resembles dao—yet spirit spear too keen.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Cheng once told Wang Yan, "You resemble the Dao in form, yet your spirit edge is too sharp."

sentences.zh: 」衍曰：「誠不如卿落落穆穆然也。

translations.literal: " Yan said: "Truly not equal you falling-falling solemn-solemn thus.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan replied, "I truly cannot match your spacious calm."

sentences.zh: 」澄由是顯名。

translations.literal: " Cheng thereby manifest fame.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Cheng rose to fame from this.

sentences.zh: 有經澄所題目者，衍不復有言，輒云「已經平子矣」。

translations.literal: Those passed Cheng's evaluation—Yan again had no words—always said "already passed Pingzi."
translations.idiomatic: When someone had passed Wang Cheng's judgment, Wang Yan said nothing more—only, "Pingzi has spoken."

sentences.zh: 少曆顯位，累遷成都王穎從事中郎。

translations.literal: Youth passed prominent posts—accumulated promoted Prince Chengdu Ying aide-de-camp.
translations.idiomatic: He rose early through high posts to aide-de-camp to Prince Sima Ying of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 穎嬖豎孟玖譖殺陸機兄弟，天下切齒。

translations.literal: Ying favorite slave Meng Jiu slandered killed Lu Ji brothers—under-heaven grind teeth.
translations.idiomatic: Ying's favorite Meng Jiu slandered the Lu brothers to their deaths—the realm gnashed its teeth.

sentences.zh: 澄發玖私奸，勸穎殺玖，穎乃誅之，士庶莫不稱善。

translations.literal: Cheng exposed Jiu private wicked—urged Ying kill Jiu—Ying then executed him—gentlemen common none not praised good.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Cheng exposed Meng's secret crimes and urged Ying to kill him; Ying did so, and all praised it.

sentences.zh: 及穎敗，東海王越請為司空長史。

translations.literal: When Ying defeated—Prince Donghai Yue requested Minister of Works chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: After Ying fell, Prince Sima Yue of Donghai named him chief clerk to the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 以迎大駕勳，封南鄉侯。

translations.literal: By welcoming grand carriage merit—enfeoffed Nanxiang marquis.
translations.idiomatic: For escorting the imperial train he was enfeoffed marquis of Nanxiang.

sentences.zh: 遷建威將軍、雍州刺史，不之職。

translations.literal: Promoted General Who Establishes Might—Yongzhou regional inspector—not took post.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted General Who Establishes Might and regional inspector of Yongzhou but did not take up the post.

sentences.zh: 時王敦、謝鯤、庾敳、阮修皆為衍所親善，號為四友，而亦與澄狎，又有光逸、胡毋輔之等亦豫焉。

translations.literal: At time Wang Dun Xie Kun Yu Kai Ruan Xiu all by Yan intimate good—called four friends—yet also with Cheng intimate—also You Guang Hu Wuzhizi etc. also joined.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun, Xie Kun, Yu Kai, and Ruan Xiu were Wang Yan's intimates, styled the Four Friends; they were also close to Wang Cheng, with Guang Yi, Hu Wuzhizi, and others joining in.

sentences.zh: 酣宴縱誕，窮歡極娛。

translations.literal: Drunk banquet unrestrained wild—exhaust joy utmost pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: They feasted and caroused without restraint, reveling to the utmost.

sentences.zh: 惠帝末，衍白越以澄為荊州刺史、持節、都督，領南蠻校尉，敦為青州。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui end—Yan told Yue take Cheng Jingzhou regional inspector—hold credentials—area command—concurrently Colonel Southern Man—Dun Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Emperor Hui's reign Wang Yan asked Yue to appoint Wang Cheng regional inspector of Jingzhou with credentials and area command plus Colonel of the Southern Man, and Wang Dun to Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 衍因問以方略，敦曰：「當臨事制變，不可豫論。

translations.literal: Yan therefore asked with scheme strategy—Dun said: "Ought face affair control change—cannot advance discuss.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan asked their strategy; Wang Dun said, "Respond as events demand—do not plan ahead."

sentences.zh: 」澄辭義鋒出，算略無方，一坐嗟服。

translations.literal: " Cheng rhetoric sharp emerged—calculation strategy without pattern—whole seated sigh admired.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Cheng's reply flashed with wit and stratagem beyond reckoning; the whole company sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 澄將之鎮，送者傾朝。

translations.literal: Cheng about go garrison—senders tilt court.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Cheng left for his post the entire court turned out to see him off.

sentences.zh: 澄見樹上鵲巢，便脫衣上樹，探而弄之，神氣蕭然，傍若無人。

translations.literal: Cheng saw tree above magpie nest—then removed clothes climbed tree—probe and play it—spirit bearing calm—beside as no person.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing a magpie nest in a tree, he stripped, climbed up, and toyed with it, utterly at ease as if alone.

sentences.zh: 劉琨謂澄曰：「卿形雖散朗，而內實動俠，以此處世，難得其死。

translations.literal: Liu Kun told Cheng: "Your form although scattered bright—inside actual stirring knight—by this dwell world—hard obtain good death.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun told him, "You seem open and free but inside you ride restless courage—with such conduct you will be hard put to die well."

sentences.zh: 」澄默然不答。

translations.literal: " Cheng silent not answered.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Cheng said nothing.

sentences.zh: 澄既至鎮，日夜縱酒，不親庶事，雖寇戎急務，亦不以在懷。

translations.literal: Cheng already arrived garrison—day night unrestrained wine—not personally attend multitude affairs—although bandit war urgent tasks—also not take in breast.
translations.idiomatic: Once at his post Wang Cheng drank day and night and ignored routine business—even urgent defense matters left him unmoved.

sentences.zh: 擢順陽人郭舒於寒悴之中，以為別駕，委以州府。

translations.literal: Raised Shunyang man Guo Shu from cold wretched—made aide—entrusted state offices.
translations.idiomatic: He raised Guo Shu of Shunyang from poverty and cold to aide and entrusted him with the provincial offices.

sentences.zh: 時京師危逼，澄率眾軍，將赴國難，而飄風折其節柱。

translations.literal: At time capital peril pressed—Cheng led crowd armies—about go state hardship—yet whirlwind broke his credentials pillar.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital was imperiled Wang Cheng led troops to the rescue, but a gale snapped his standard pole.

sentences.zh: 會王如寇襄陽，澄前鋒至宜城，遣使詣山簡，為如党嚴嶷所獲。

translations.literal: When Wang Ru raided Xiangyang—Cheng vanguard reached Yicheng—sent envoy to Shan Jian—by Ru faction Yan Yi captured.
translations.idiomatic: As Wang Ru struck Xiangyang, Wang Cheng's vanguard reached Yicheng; envoys to Shan Jian were seized by Yan Yi, Wang Ru's ally.

sentences.zh: 嶷偽使人從襄陽來而問之曰：「襄陽拔未？

translations.literal: Yi feigned sent person from Xiangyang come and asked: "Xiangyang taken yet?
translations.idiomatic: Yan Yi planted a fake messenger from Xiangyang who asked, "Has Xiangyang fallen?"

sentences.zh: 」答云：「昨旦破城，已獲山簡。

translations.literal: " Answered: "Yesterday dawn broke city—already captured Shan Jian.
translations.idiomatic: The reply: "It fell this morning—Shan Jian is taken."

sentences.zh: 」乃陰緩澄使，令得亡去。

translations.literal: " Thereupon secretly slack Cheng envoy—ordered able flee go.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Yi quietly let Wang Cheng's envoy slip away.

sentences.zh: 澄聞襄陽陷，以為信然，散眾而還。

translations.literal: Cheng heard Xiangyang fell—thought trustworthy—dispersed crowds returned.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Xiangyang had fallen, Wang Cheng believed it and dismissed his army.

sentences.zh: 既而恥之，托糧運不贍，委罪長史蔣俊而斬之，竟不能進。

translations.literal: Before long shamed it—pretext grain transport not sufficient—delegate blame chief clerk Jiang Jun and executed him—ended could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed afterward, he blamed lack of supplies, pinned fault on chief clerk Jiang Jun, executed him, and never advanced.

sentences.zh: 巴蜀流人散在荊、湘者，與土人忿爭，遂殺縣令，屯聚樂鄉。

translations.literal: Ba Shu vagabonds scattered at Jing Xiang—with natives anger quarrel—thereupon killed county magistrate—gathered garrison Lexiang.
translations.idiomatic: Ba–Shu refugees scattered through Jing and Xiang quarreled with locals, slew a county magistrate, and massed at Lexiang.

sentences.zh: 澄使成都內史王機討之。

translations.literal: Cheng sent Chengdu interior steward Wang Ji campaign them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Cheng ordered Wang Ji, interior steward of Chengdu, to attack them.

sentences.zh: 賊請降，澄偽許之，既而襲之於寵洲，以其妻子為賞，沈八千餘人于江中。

translations.literal: Bandits sought surrender—Cheng falsely promised—before long attacked them at Chong Isle—took their wives children as rewards—sank eight thousand odd men in river.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels asked to yield; Wang Cheng feigned consent, then ambushed them at Chong Isle, seized their families as spoil, and drowned more than eight thousand in the river.

sentences.zh: 於是益、梁流人四五萬家一時俱反，推杜弢為主，，南破零桂，東掠武昌，敗王機于巴陵。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yi Liang vagabonds four five myriad households one time all rebelled—raised Du Tao as lord——south broke Ling Gui—east raided Wuchang—defeated Wang Ji at Baling.
translations.idiomatic: Then forty or fifty thousand refugee households in Yi and Liang rose together, made Du Tao their chief, smashed Ling and Gui in the south, raided Wuchang in the east, and defeated Wang Ji at Baling.

sentences.zh: 澄亦無憂懼之意，但與機日夜縱酒，投壺博戲，數十局俱起。

translations.literal: Cheng also no worry fear intent—but with Ji day night unrestrained wine—throw pot gamble games—several tens rounds all rise.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Cheng showed no alarm; he and Wang Ji drank day and night, played pitch-pot and gambling games, round after round.

sentences.zh: 殺富人李才，取其家資以賜郭舒。

translations.literal: Killed rich man Li Cai—took his house wealth to grant Guo Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He slew the rich man Li Cai, seized his assets, and gave them to Guo Shu.

sentences.zh: 南平太守應詹驟諫，不納。

translations.literal: Nanping grand warden Ying Zhan repeatedly remonstrated—not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Nanping grand warden Ying Zhan remonstrated again and again; Wang Cheng ignored him.

sentences.zh: 於是上下離心，內外怨叛。

translations.literal: Thereupon above below separate hearts—inner outer resent rebel.
translations.idiomatic: High and low turned against him; inside and outside grew bitter and mutinous.

sentences.zh: 澄望實雖損，猶傲然自得。

translations.literal: Cheng reputation substance although harmed—still proud self satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: Though his reputation suffered, Wang Cheng remained smugly pleased with himself.

sentences.zh: 後出軍擊杜弢，次於作塘。

translations.literal: Later went army strike Du Tao—halted at Zuotang.
translations.idiomatic: Later he marched against Du Tao and halted at Zuotang.

sentences.zh: 山簡參軍王沖叛於豫州，自稱荊州刺史。

translations.literal: Shan Jian aide Wang Chong rebelled at Yuzhou—self titled Jingzhou regional inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Jian's aide Wang Chong rebelled in Yuzhou and proclaimed himself regional inspector of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 澄懼，使杜蕤守江陵。

translations.literal: Cheng feared—sent Du Rui guard Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Cheng grew afraid and posted Du Rui to defend Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 澄遷於孱陵，尋奔遝中。

translations.literal: Cheng moved to Chanling—soon fled Tao middle.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Cheng withdrew to Chanling, then fled into the interior.

sentences.zh: 郭舒諫曰：「使君臨州，雖無異政，未失眾心。

translations.literal: Guo Shu remonstrated: "Lord faces province—although no unusual governance—not lost crowd hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Shu remonstrated: "Since you took this province you have done nothing remarkable, yet you have not lost the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 今西收華容向義之兵，足以擒此小丑，奈何自棄。

translations.literal: Now west gather Huarong toward righteousness troops—sufficient capture this petty clown—why self abandon.
translations.idiomatic: Gather loyal troops west at Huarong and you can seize this petty villain—why abandon yourself?"

sentences.zh: 」澄不能從。

translations.literal: " Cheng could not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Cheng would not listen.

sentences.zh: 初，澄命武陵諸郡同討杜弢，天門太守扈瑰次於益陽。

translations.literal: Initially—Cheng ordered Wuling various commanderies together campaign Du Tao—Tianmen grand warden Hu Gui halted at Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wang Cheng had ordered the Wuling commanderies jointly to strike Du Tao; Tianmen grand warden Hu Gui camped at Yiyang.

translations.idiomatic: Wherever Guang ruled he won no flashy praise, yet each time he left office lingering kindness won remembrance.
